title: Infinitesimal conjugacy of split diagonalizable homomorphisms over rings
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $J\subseteq A$ an ideal with $J^2=0$, and $A_0=A/J$. Put $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $M$ be a finitely generated abelian group and $H=D_A(M)=\operatorname{Spec}A[M]$ with the Hopf operations of [def-sfb-ring-diagonalizable-group]. Let $G$ be a smooth affine $S$-group scheme of finite presentation [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]; its group operations satisfy the group diagrams as specified in [def-sfb-ring-diagonalizable-group]. Let $f_1,f_2:H\to G$ be $S$-group homomorphisms whose base changes to $\operatorname{Spec}A_0$ [def-pc-base-change] are equal. Then there exists $u\in\ker(G(A)\to G(A_0))$ such that $\operatorname{Int}(u)\circ f_1=f_2$ as $S$-group homomorphisms, where $\operatorname{Int}(u)(g)=ugu^{-1}$ on every test algebra. Neither homomorphism is assumed injective. No Noetherian, local, field, reducedness, connectedness, or torsion-freeness hypothesis is imposed; in particular torsion in $M$ may have order noninvertible in $A$, and $M=0$ and $J=0$ are allowed.

source.place: Conrad, Reductive group schemes (2014), Proposition B.2.5, printed pp.286–287, Corollary B.2.6, printed p.287, and Remark B.2.4, printed p.285: conjugacy classes of supplied lifts are a torsor under regular H^1, which vanishes for diagonalizable groups. Read online; WANTED locally as literature/conrad-reductive-group-schemes.pdf. No Stacks tag states this conjugacy theorem.

proof.text: Put $N=\ker(G(A)\to G(A/J))$, with the additive module structure of [lem-sfb-group-space-square-zero-kernel-module]. Write $C=A[M]$ and $C_2=A[M\oplus M]$. Their bases $e_m$ and $e_{(m,n)}$ are given by [def-sfb-ring-diagonalizable-group]. They are free over $A$: tensoring an exact sequence with either algebra is a direct sum of copies of that sequence and is exact. Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-group-congruence-flat-scalar-extension] to obtain $K_C=N\otimes_A C$ and $K_{C_2}=N\otimes_A C_2$, where $K_B=\ker(G(B)\to G(B/JB))$ and products in each kernel are sums. These tensor modules identify with finite coefficient families indexed by $M$ and $M\oplus M$: the inverse to $(n_m)\mapsto\sum_m n_m\otimes e_m$ sends $n\otimes\sum_m a_me_m$ to $(a_mn)_m$, by the bilinear universal property of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. The cited scalar-extension theorem supplies naturality even for nonflat maps between these flat algebras, and linearity of conjugation.

source.place: Conrad, Reductive group schemes, Proposition B.2.5 (final paragraph), printed pp.286--287, and Corollary B.2.6 with Remark B.2.4, printed pp.285,287; read online. Agent explicit group-algebra coefficient argument; local copy WANTED as literature/conrad-reductive-group-schemes.pdf.

proof.text:
Let $x$ be the universal $H$-point over $C$, and let $x,y$ be its two extensions over $C_2$ via $e_m\mapsto e_{(m,0)}$ and $e_m\mapsto e_{(0,m)}$. The coproduct of [def-sfb-ring-diagonalizable-group] gives $xy$ via $e_m\mapsto e_{(m,m)}$. Define $c(x)=f_2(x)f_1(x)^{-1}\in K_C$, since the reductions of $f_1,f_2$ agree. Write $\rho_x$ for conjugation by $f_1(x)$. The homomorphism identities give
$$f_2(xy)f_1(xy)^{-1}=c(x)f_1(x)c(y)f_1(x)^{-1}.$$
Using the additive kernels and substitution naturality of [lem-sfb-smooth-group-congruence-flat-scalar-extension], this is
$$c(xy)=c(x)+\rho_x(c(y))\quad\text{in }N\otimes_A C_2.$$

source.place: Conrad, Reductive group schemes, Proposition B.2.5 (final paragraph), printed pp.286--287, and Corollary B.2.6 with Remark B.2.4, printed pp.285,287; read online. Agent explicit group-algebra coefficient argument; local copy WANTED as literature/conrad-reductive-group-schemes.pdf.

proof.text: Write $c(y)=\sum_{m\in M}n_m e_m(y)$ with finite support and set $p=n_0\in N$. Take the coefficient of $e_0(y)$ in the preceding identity, treating $N\otimes_A C_2$ as finite sums in the $y$-basis with coefficients in $N\otimes_A C$. The left side is $\sum_m n_m e_m(x)e_m(y)$ and has coefficient $p$. The first right-hand term is independent of $y$, so its coefficient is $c(x)$. By [lem-sfb-smooth-group-congruence-flat-scalar-extension], conjugation over $C_2$ is the scalar extension of conjugation over $C$ and is $C_2$-linear. Thus $\rho_x(c(y))=\sum_m e_m(y)\rho_x(n_m)$ has coefficient $\rho_x(p)$. Consequently $c(x)=p-\rho_x(p)$. The basis indexed by $M$ distinguishes every $m$ from $0$ unless $m=0$, regardless of torsion; no division or reducedness is used.

source.place: Conrad, Reductive group schemes, Proposition B.2.5 (final paragraph), printed pp.286--287, and Corollary B.2.6 with Remark B.2.4, printed pp.285,287; read online. Agent explicit group-algebra coefficient argument; local copy WANTED as literature/conrad-reductive-group-schemes.pdf.

proof.text: Regard $p$ as the point $u\in N\subseteq G(A)$. The normalization at $A$ in [lem-sfb-smooth-group-congruence-flat-scalar-extension] identifies its extension to $C$ with the constant coefficient $p$. In the additive kernel, $p-\rho_x(p)$ therefore represents $u f_1(x)u^{-1}f_1(x)^{-1}$. Since it equals $c(x)=f_2(x)f_1(x)^{-1}$, cancellation in $G(C)$ gives $u f_1(x)u^{-1}=f_2(x)$. This equality at the universal point is equality of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}C\to G$: composing either morphism with the identity $C$-point returns that morphism, using [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Every other test point is its pullback. Hence $\operatorname{Int}(u)\circ f_1=f_2$ as $S$-group homomorphisms, and $u$ reduces to the identity by its membership in $N$.

Step 1: A[M] and A[M⊕M] are free, so the flat scalar-extension lemma gives K_C=N⊗C and K_{C_2}=N⊗C_2. Step 2: c=f_2f_1^{-1} on the universal point lies in K_C because f_1 and f_2 agree on A_0[M]. The identity c(xy)=c(x)+ρ_x(c(y)) holds, with the coproduct maps e_m↦e_{(m,0)}, e_{(0,m)}, e_{(m,m)}. Torsion in M causes no problem and nothing is divided. Step 4: u=p∈K_A gives u f_1(x) u^{-1}=f_2(x); since x is the identity of Spec C, this is equality of morphisms, and u reduces to 1. Edge cases J=0, M=0, A=0, M=Z/p in characteristic p and f_1 trivial all check out.
